                           Passage: Family Contrasts

 At the family talent show, my naïve little brother thought everyone would win a
  prize. My aunt, an adept and agile dancer, performed beautifully. My uncle,
  however, didn't scowl at his own clumsy attempt; he laughed. We all agreed
                   his idea for a comedy act was far from trite.



Apply What You Have Learned About Antonym
      Antonym context clues are words around a difficult word that mean
      the opposite or nearly the opposite as the word.
Directions: Select the word that most closely matches the underlined word in
the sentence. Use the antonym in red as clue to the correct meaning.


   1. We thought it was a brilliant idea, but our teacher thought it was trite.
             a. special b. loud            c. common           d. happy
   2. Mr. Lim is adept with crossword puzzles, while his wife is terrible at
      solving.
      a. awful         b. lazy      c. skilled      d. bored
   3. Mother was suspicious when Danny handed her the bag, but my naïve
      little sister opened it anyway.
      a. Sad             b. careful           c. trusting         d. demanding
   4. Rather than scowl, dad had a huge smile on his face.
